wu: Warm-up: 'Simon Says' with Halloween commands. Teacher says 'Simon says touch your nose,' 'Simon says say boo,' 'Simon says pretend to be a witch.' Students react physically and repeat the words.
wuAlt: Warm-up: 'What's Missing?' with 3 Halloween flashcards (pumpkin, witch, ghost) on the board. Students close eyes, teacher removes one, they guess which is missing.
Warm-up: 'Action Chant' - Teacher chants 'Pumpkin, pumpkin, round and orange!' with gestures, students repeat and copy gestures.
pres: Presentation: Show large flashcards of pumpkin, witch, ghost. Say 'It is a pumpkin. It has got a big face.' Repeat for witch and ghost. Point to features (hat, broom, sheet) and ask 'What has it got?' Students answer 'It has got a hat.'
presAlt: Presentation: Use a Halloween storybook with big pictures. Read 'Look! A ghost. It has got a white sheet.' Point to the sheet, ask students to repeat.
Presentation: Teacher wears a witch hat and says 'I am a witch. I have got a hat.' Pass the hat to students, each says 'I am a witch. I have got a hat.'
prac: Guided practice: 'Matching Race' - Two teams race to match word cards (pumpkin, witch, ghost) with picture cards. Teacher says 'Find the witch!' Students grab the correct pair. Winners get high-fives.
pracAlt: Guided practice: 'Have Got Drill' - Teacher shows a ghost flashcard, asks 'What has it got?' Students say 'It has got a sheet.' Repeat with witch and pumpkin.
Guided practice: 'Pair Work' - Student A holds a flashcard, Student B asks 'What has it got?' Student A answers 'It has got a [feature].' Swap roles.
ls: Listening slot: Listen to a simple story about a ghost, witch, and pumpkin. Story: 'The ghost has got a sheet. The witch has got a hat. The pumpkin has got a face.' Students listen and sequence 3 picture cards in the correct order.
re: Reactivation game: 'Halloween Freeze Dance' - Play spooky music, students dance when music plays. Teacher pauses music and shouts 'Ghost!' Students freeze and say 'It has got a sheet!'
prod: Production task: 'Create a Halloween Character' - Students draw a witch, ghost, or pumpkin. They present their drawing to the class, saying 'This is a witch. It has got a hat and a broom.'
rw: Reading and writing slot: Students read 3 simple sentences on a worksheet: 'The pumpkin has got a face.' 'The ghost has got a sheet.' 'The witch has got a hat.' They match each sentence to the correct character picture. Then, they trace the sentences and copy them once.
st: Story / song + goodbye: Read a short Halloween story with repetition. End with 'Goodbye Song' where students sing 'Goodbye, goodbye, see you next time!' Teacher gives stickers and students line up for high-fives.
g: Teams race to match word cards with picture cards.
Teacher gives commands with Halloween words, students react.
Teacher removes a flashcard, students guess which one is missing.
Students dance and freeze when music stops, saying a character's feature.
Students draw a character and present it using 'It has got...'
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Draw two characters and write two sentences about each.
Support / weaker learners: Use sentence starters like 'It has got a...' to complete the worksheet.
hw: Homework option 1: Teach the words pumpkin, witch, ghost, and 'It has got...' to a family member and draw a picture.
Homework option 2: Practice the 'I am from Morocco' chant with a family member.
Homework option 3: Color a Halloween picture and label it with the words.
tip: Tip: Use TPR (Total Physical Response) for vocabulary retention—students remember words better when paired with gestures. For the American Space Oujda context, connect Halloween to local celebrations like Eid by comparing festive foods or costumes.
